event: Nala reads her Status through again, slowly, in wonder.
prose: You go back to the top and read it all again, slowly, line by line. A Status. Your Status, with a Class and Attributes and Paths, sitting in your mind in plain words.

event: She wonders what a Path is, and what Soulstealing and the Completionist will ask of her.
prose: What is a Path? A road you walk, or something that walks you? Soulstealing sounds like what you just did to the demon. Exceptionalism sounds like homework you already aced. You turn the words over and get nothing back from them.

event: She leaves the two Unallocated Stats unspent.
prose: Talented sits there too, a shiny one hundred beside it. You don't know enough yet to know what it does.

memory.fact: Talented sits on her Status at 100, and she doesn't yet know what it does.

event: The wonder wears thin; in the warm dark there is nothing to do but wait.
prose: After a while the words stop feeling new. The dark is warm and the heartbeat keeps time, and you can't see, or move much, or go anywhere. You are bored.

event: To pass the time she counts in her head: one, two, three, on and on.
prose: So you count. One, two, three, four. Past fifty, past a hundred, on into the hundreds, one number after the next.

memory.fact: Bored in the womb, she passed the time counting in her head, on into the hundreds.

event: She counts up by twos, then by threes, then back down again.
prose: You keep counting. Up by twos: two, four, six, eight. Up by threes: three, six, nine, twelve. Then back down the same ladders, to zero.

event: She moves on to multiples, up and down: sevens, then nines, then twelves.
prose: Then multiples. Sevens, up and down: seven, fourteen, twenty-one, twenty-eight. Nines next, then twelves, up past a hundred and forty-four and back down again, while the heartbeat thumps on.

event: Muffled through the walls, many women's voices start a chant in words she doesn't know.
prose:
:::status-assessment
name: Path of Basic Numeracy
note: Tier: 2; Mental: +1
:::

Somewhere past the walls, voices start up. Muffled, many of them, women's voices, chanting the same words together. You don't know the words.
